title: Multi-City Live Theater in VR: Uncanny Alley (Ferryman Collective)
description: The Emmy-winning live VR show Uncanny Alley: A New Day plays at Gray Area and in Los Angeles at the same time, with one cast across both cities and audience members joining onstage in headsets. Afterwards there's a backstage tour of the tech. Hosted by the SF SIGGRAPH chapters.

title: San Francisco Singles Speed Dating Game Night (30s/40s)
description: Activity-based singles night: table icebreaker games like 'Friendly Feud' instead of straight speed dating, with private matching afterwards. The Nov 10 date is for singles in their 30s/40s.

title: Drop-In Circling Workshop (Berkeley)
description: The Circling Institute's in-person drop-in evening of the Original Circling approach and authentic relating, a guided practice in presence and deep connection with strangers. It's the closest in-person circling to SF this month, and the last one sold out a week ahead. East Bay: BART to Downtown Berkeley (~25 min), then bus or bike to West Berkeley.

title: Conundrum Chronicles StorySlam: Turning Point
description: A monthly true-story slam on the theme 'Turning Point', with featured storyteller Kimberlii Joy. Put your name in the hat to tell a five-minute story without notes, or just listen; everyone in the room can judge.

title: KQED Live: Paint, Sip & Play - a Mission District lotería night
description: Paint your own lotería board, then play a game of Mission Lotería whose cards tell the history of the Mission District. Drag Laureate Per Sia performs, and one of the neighborhood's cultural keepers tells the stories behind the cards.

title: Entangled Intelligences (Long Now: Eagleman, Lanier, Levin and more)
address: Pier 2, Fort Mason Center, San Francisco, CA 94123
description: A Long Now special evening on interspecies and synthetic intelligence, with David Eagleman, Jaron Lanier, Michael Levin, Sara Imari Walker and others plus performers. It runs from microbes and ecosystems to AI agents and exoplanets. It was sold out with a waitlist in late October; Eventbrite showed tickets back in stock on 1 Nov — book promptly.

title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong at SF Playhouse
description: The Mischief farce (from the makers of The Play That Goes Wrong): an amateur troupe's Peter Pan collapses into slapstick chaos. Final run, to Nov 28; Tuesdays 7pm. Funcheap lists a $5-off code.

title: Do I Want Kids? A Psychology-Based Guide to Figuring It Out
description: SOLD OUT. Big Brain lecture-in-a-bar: a psychology-based guide to deciding whether you want kids — research on values, regret and decision-making.

title: Claudio Simonetti's Goblin performs the live score to Tenebre
description: Goblin, the Italian prog band behind the Suspiria and Dawn of the Dead scores, perform their soundtrack live to a screening of Dario Argento's 1982 giallo Tenebre in the Castro's movie palace.

title: Woodchopper's Ball: Neil Fontano Jazz Band
description: The weekly Tuesday live-band swing dance at the historic Verdi Club, this week with the Neil Fontano Jazz Band. The free drop-in beginner lesson at 9pm is included, and no partner is needed.

title: Dinner: Let's talk about the AI crisis (talk by Prof. David Krueger)
description: Free dumplings-and-discussion evening from Firebell, a new AI-risk society: a 6:15pm talk by AI professor David Krueger on the state of AI risk, Q&A, then dinner and open discussion (veg/vegan/GF options). East Bay: BART from Montgomery to Downtown Berkeley (~25 min), then ~10 min by bike to Fourth St.

title: Let's talk about Power Concentration!
venue: San Francisco (address on Luma after registering)
description: Discussion evening on AI and power concentration, listed on both the Mox and AI Safety SF calendars (address shared with registrants — likely Mox in the Mission).

title: Trivia Night at Manny's
description: Manny's free second-Wednesday pub-style trivia with drinks. It's a relaxed way to join a team and meet people in the Mission.

title: Big Brain Bay Area: What Happens When a Country Gets Hacked? Cyberwar and the Systems We Depend On
description: A lecture-in-a-bar talk by Nate Gleason, who leads Lawrence Livermore's cyber and infrastructure resilience programme. It covers how attacks on grids, water and ports become physical, 'immune infrastructure', and how AI is changing both attack and defence.

title: 2nd Wednesday Balkan Folk Dancing at Ashkenaz
description: Ashkenaz's long-running Balkan line and circle dance night (Macedonian, Bulgarian, Romanian, Albanian, Romani). A beginner-friendly lesson at 7pm with Nadav Nur and Susie Shoaf, then open dancing until 10pm, and no partner needed. East Bay: BART to North Berkeley (~25 min from Montgomery), then a ~20 min walk or AC Transit 72.

title: San Francisco Wednesday Contra Dance (beginner lesson 7:30)
description: BACDS contra with caller Sarah Trop and the band Pizzatron 3000. Beginner lesson at 7:30, then dancing to live music until 10pm. Gender-neutral roles, no partner needed.

title: Jake Xerxes Fussell with Dougie Poole
description: Jake Xerxes Fussell is one of the best interpreters of old American folk songs working today, supported by left-field country songwriter Dougie Poole. The show is fully seated. Doors 7pm.

title: Arab Film Festival: Chronicle of a Disappearance (Elia Suleiman)
description: The Arab Film Festival's Roxie night closes with Elia Suleiman's deadpan, tableau-style 1996 classic about returning to Palestine. A 6pm Palestinian Voices shorts program plays the same evening.

title: Lila Forde: Life Can Still Be Sweet Tour, with Hazle Nova
description: Seattle-born, LA-based singer-songwriter Lila Forde plays jazz-, soul- and folk-rooted Americana in an intimate North Beach listening room. Doors 7:30pm, all ages.

title: Exploratorium After Dark: Unplug and Play
address: Pier 15, The Embarcadero at Green St, San Francisco, CA 94111
description: The monthly social After Dark: Roryography dance session, science trivia, a debate on alien consciousness and 650+ hands-on exhibits. It's adults only (18+) and billed as a night to 'find your community'.

title: Cal Academy NightLife: Pajammy Jam (21+)
address: 55 Music Concourse Dr, Golden Gate Park, San Francisco, CA 94118
description: A pajama-themed house-party NightLife with games, music and the aquarium and rainforest open after hours. It's 21+, and planetarium shows are $7 extra.

title: Little Forest: screening + conversation with director Yim Soon-rye
description: Screening of the much-loved 2018 Korean foodie film Little Forest, followed by a conversation with director Yim Soon-rye in person, one of South Korea's leading auteurs. Presented with the Korean Cultural Center LA, alongside the RM x SFMOMA exhibition.

title: Mark Danner: Crossing the Rubicon, in conversation with Guy Marzorati
description: Journalist and MacArthur Fellow Mark Danner discusses his collected essays tracing the erosion of American democratic institutions from Bush v. Gore to 2026, with KQED's Guy Marzorati. The talk is in the store at the landmark Beat-era bookshop.

title: Talent Show: Has Mox Got Talent?
description: The rationalist/AI-safety community space hosts a talent show of music, magic, comedy and odd skills like speed-cubing and mental math. All are welcome, and it's an easy way to meet the Mox crowd. (Moved from 29 Oct to 12 Nov.)

title: KQED Live: Object Stories San Francisco
description: Bay Area artists, makers and community voices each bring a handmade object that matters to them and tell its story. It's the American Craft Council's storytelling series, co-presented by KQED.

title: Points of Departure: Life on the Water reunion (Fort Mason)
venue: Bayfront Theater, Fort Mason Center (Building B, 3rd floor)
description: The founders of Life on the Water, the experimental performance company that ran this stage from 1986 to 1993 (Ellen Sebastian Chang, Bill Talen aka Reverend Billy, Leonard Pitt, Joe Lambert), reunite for a conversation plus rare performance video. Reserve space on the Fort Mason page.

title: Arab Film Festival Under the Stars: Spices and Lies (free outdoor screening)
description: The 30th Arab Film Festival's first-ever outdoor screening is Spices and Lies, a French-Algerian romantic comedy starring Hiam Abbas. Shawarma and kunafa vendors are on site in Hayes Valley's open-air PROXY lot.

title: Mahal Mural Unveiling + mini block party (SoMa Filipinas)
description: UNDSCVRD SF unveils two large new murals in the Filipino Cultural District alley. A free block party follows, with art activities, a fashion show and love-song karaoke.

title: Kevin Starr Lecture: (Re)interpreting Anza 250 (SF Historical Society)
description: The SF Historical Society's 8th annual Kevin Starr Lecture: a panel on the legacy and conflicts of the 1776 Anza Expedition, which led to the founding of the Presidio and Mission Dolores. The reception is at 6pm and the lecture at 6:30.

title: Pyramid Dance // Ean Golden
venue: Unitarian Universalist Society of San Francisco
description: A Friday-night conscious dance from the MOVEMENT ecstatic-dance crew, with DJ Ean Golden on a BASSBOSS surround system plus tea service and organic food. Phone-free and substance-free.

title: 5Rhythms Wild Release (Friday night wave)
description: Weekly Friday 5Rhythms wave in the Mission, taught this week by Alessandro Moruzzi. It's substance-free and barefoot, beginners welcome. Doors close at 7:30pm.

title: Janet Thornburg's Cognitive Divine (solo comedy)
description: Solo show in which one performer plays seven sub-personalities arguing over whether to stay in San Francisco. It won Best Full-Length Comedy at the Marsh's 2026 In Front of Your Eyes festival. Fridays at 7:30pm, Nov 6-Dec 11; 60 minutes.

title: The Moth GrandSLAM Championship
description: Winners of the Bay Area's Moth StorySLAMs compete to be crowned San Francisco GrandSLAM storytelling champion. True stories told live without notes. [SOLD OUT as of 1 Nov — waitlist only.]

title: Dos Bandoleros (and friends): rumba flamenca at The Lost Church
description: Bay Area Spanish-guitar duo playing Gipsy Kings-style rumba flamenca with Latin rhythms, then a second set with guests, in North Beach's listening room. Doors 7:30pm.

title: Other Lives with Kelcey Ayer
description: Oklahoma's cinematic indie-folk band, with Local Natives' Kelcey Ayer opening (folkYEAH! presents). Doors 8pm.

title: Fall SF International Tea Festival
description: Unlimited tastings from 30+ international tea vendors (Vietnamese, Nepali, Kenyan, Korean, Wuyishan oolongs and more), and you keep a porcelain tasting cup. It also runs Sun Nov 15.

title: Renegade Craft Holiday Fair San Francisco
description: A big holiday craft fair with 250+ curated independent makers on the waterfront at Fort Mason. It also runs Sunday Nov 15, 11am-5pm.

title: SF City Guides free walking tour: Scandalous Murals of Rincon Center
description: A free volunteer-led indoor tour of the controversial WPA-era murals in the former Rincon Annex post office, a few blocks from home. The meeting point is the east end of the historic lobby near Mission & Steuart.

title: Relish Speed Dating (ages 29-42)
description: A Saturday-evening speed-dating round of 5-7 minute mini-dates with 8-12 singles aged 29-42, held in a FiDi hotel lounge. Picks go in on your phone and matches arrive the next day.

title: Root Division: New Works 2026 opening reception
description: Opening of Root Division's biennial survey of its studio artists: drawing, painting, sculpture, photography and multimedia. Itzel Rios-Ellis's solo show Under the Orchidian Beam opens in the mezzanine at the same time. A sociable SoMa opening a few minutes from home.

title: Abiogenesis: Philip Beesley & Casey Curran opening (SF Art Week)
description: Free opening reception for a two-artist show of kinetic, light-responsive sculpture about life emerging from inert matter. It's part of SF Art Week, and Philip Beesley represented Canada at the Venice Architecture Biennale.

title: San Francisco English Country Dance (2nd Saturday)
price: $20 ($15 members, $6 students; pay what you can)
description: BACDS's monthly SF English country dance with caller Nick Cuccia and live music from Betsy St. Aubin, Craig Johnson and Michele Winter. A workshop starts at 7:15pm, so it's beginner-friendly.

title: BATS Improv: Theatresports
venue: BATS Bayfront Theatre, Fort Mason Center
address: 2 Marina Blvd, Building B, 3rd Floor, San Francisco, CA 94123
description: BATS's long-running improv competition: teams battle through scenes and games judged by the audience. Saturdays at 8pm Nov 7, 14, 21 and 28.

title: A Night of Live Local Roots Music: Ben Grant, Magpie, The Spare Keys
description: Three local folk/roots acts at the Hotel Utah Saloon, a short walk from home. A cheap Saturday folk night in a historic bar.

title: The Cactus Blossoms with Margo Cilker
description: Minneapolis brothers The Cactus Blossoms play Everly-style close-harmony country-folk, with Oregon songwriter Margo Cilker opening. Presented by (((folkYEAH!))). Doors 8pm.

title: Sean Hayes (album release) with KATZROAR and Etienne de Rocher
description: Album-release show from SF's long-time folk-soul songwriter Sean Hayes, with Oakland's KATZROAR and Etienne de Rocher (Haunted Shed). Doors 8:30pm, 21+.

title: MOVEMENT Ecstatic Dance SF // Sasha Rose
description: The weekly Sunday ecstatic dance at Sacred Heart, this week with DJ Sasha Rose. It's phone-free and substance-free, opening with a circle before a long DJ journey.

title: Lindy in the Park: free swing dancing + beginner lesson
venue: Golden Gate Park, JFK Drive (8th-10th Ave)
address: JFK Dr between 8th & 10th Ave (behind the de Young), San Francisco, CA
description: Free outdoor swing dancing every Sunday since 1996 on car-free JFK Drive, with a free beginner lesson at noon. No partner needed; weather permitting.

title: Improv(e) Your Dating Life workshop (Endgames)
description: A two-hour workshop that mixes improv exercises with dating tips from dating coach Dylan Garcia, built around being present and widening your dating pool. A low-stakes way to try improv and meet people.

title: SF Civic Music: Mozart to Mendelssohn (with Chora Nova)
address: 401 Van Ness Ave, San Francisco, CA 94102
description: The community orchestra's free choral-orchestral program at the Herbst, including Fanny Mendelssohn Hensel's rarely heard oratorio and Grace Williams' The Dancers.

title: Playful Sunset Ocean Dance (silent disco on Ocean Beach)
venue: Ocean Beach (Great Highway at Balboa St)
address: Great Highway & Balboa St, San Francisco, CA 94121
description: A playful-themed sunset silent-disco dance on Ocean Beach with headphones provided. It's a sober, ecstatic-dance-style session on the sand.

title: Art in the Age of AI: Holly Herndon, Mat Dryhurst and Hans Ulrich Obrist
description: AI-art pioneers Holly Herndon and Mat Dryhurst talk with curator Hans Ulrich Obrist about protocol art, why artists need power over the systems they work within, and where art and AI go next. Co-presented with Villa Albertine.

title: The Secret Museum by Lynne Kaufman (with post-show talkback)
description: New four-hander about a filmmaker documenting a newly excavated Pompeii fresco with startling evidence about sex and the sacred. This Sunday show is followed by a talkback with the playwright and cast. Runs Nov 7-22, Sat 8pm and Sun 5pm; 70 minutes.

title: Julie Beth Napolin (NYC psych-folk) with Bob Bannister, Aux Meadows, Danny Paul Grody
description: An early Sunday bill of psych-folk and guitar soundscapes at the Make-Out Room: Silver Current Records' Julie Beth Napolin plus local guitarist Danny Paul Grody.

title: Rodrigo y Gabriela: OurHome Tour
description: The Grammy-winning Mexican acoustic-guitar duo plays its new album in the restored Castro Theatre. Doors 6pm; price per The List ($64.75), confirm at checkout.

title: Kate Nash with Joh Chase
description: The British indie-pop songwriter in the wood-panelled upstairs hall at 2174 Market. Doors 7pm, all ages.

title: Fog of Love learn-and-play night at The Love Potion Library
description: Dogpatch Games teaches Fog of Love, a two-player romantic-comedy board game in which you play characters who meet, fall in love and try to make it work, at the Castro's romance bookshop and tea room. All welcome; a playful way to meet someone.

title: Ben Buchanan: Superintelligence, Superpowers, and the Fate of the World
description: The first White House special advisor for AI, now an advisor to Anthropic, discusses his book The Bitter Struggle. Topics include AI CEOs' private warnings, chip export controls and how democracies should handle transformative AI. Doors at 6pm.

title: Contact Improvisation class + jam at The Castro Room
description: SF's 1st & 3rd Monday contact improv night: an hour's beginner-friendly class from 7:45pm flows into a jam with live music until 10:15pm. Teachers and hosts rotate.

title: Margaret Glaspy with Anna Tivel
description: Sharp guitar-driven indie songwriter Margaret Glaspy, with Portland folk singer Anna Tivel opening. Doors 7pm, all ages.

title: John Proctor Is the Villain (A.C.T. preview)
description: West Coast premiere of Kimberly Belflower's Tony-nominated Best Play: five Georgia high-schoolers studying The Crucible start questioning who gets called a hero, scored to pop music. Runs Nov 12-Dec 6. This Tuesday preview has cheaper preview pricing; 1h45, no interval.

title: Let’s Talk About Swarms: After the Hugging Face × OpenAI Hack
venue: San Francisco (address on Luma after registering)
description: Discussion evening on AI agent swarms and multi-agent safety, following the Hugging Face × OpenAI hackathon. Listed on both the Mox and AI Safety SF calendars; address shared with registrants (likely Mox in the Mission).

title: ChinaTalk & Unbound Book Club: Everyday Movement
description: SOLD OUT (waitlist only). ChinaTalk's monthly China Reads book club in a Chinatown bookshop-café. This month's book is Gigi Leung Lee-chi's Hong Kong protest novel Everyday Movement.

title: Philosophy Talk Live: Franz Kafka and the World Without a Path
description: Be in the live audience as KALW's Philosophy Talk records an episode on Kafka with Tulane scholar Karen Zumhagen-Yekplé. There's audience Q&A and Ian Shoales' satirical 'Sixty-Second Philosopher' segment.

title: Who’s That Under the Bridge? Patents, Trolls, and the Price of Innovation
description: Big Brain lecture-in-a-bar on patent trolls: how the patent system gets gamed, what it costs innovation, and whether reform can work.

title: Jazz at the Make-Out Room
description: A free Tuesday jazz night in the Mission bar (doors 6pm, music 7pm). An easy weeknight drop-in.

title: Silverada with Emily Nenni
description: The Texas country-rock band (formerly Mike and the Moonpies) tours its ninth album, with honky-tonk songwriter Emily Nenni opening. Doors 7:30pm, all ages.

title: Woodchopper's Ball: San Francisco Medicine Ball Band
description: The weekly Tuesday live-band swing dance at the historic Verdi Club, this week with the San Francisco Medicine Ball Band. The free drop-in beginner lesson at 9pm is included, and no partner is needed.

title: Terror Tuesday: The Exorcist (archival 35mm, original theatrical cut)
description: Alamo's weekly Terror Tuesday cult slot screens an archival 35mm print of the original theatrical cut of Friedkin's The Exorcist, long unavailable in theaters. Dinner-and-a-movie setup with food and drink served at your seat.

title: Patch Bay workshop: Computational Poetry
description: Alicia Guo leads a hands-on workshop treating language as material to be examined, shaped and animated with code. It covers the history and tools of computational poetry, part of Gray Area's weekly Patch Bay creative-tech night.

title: Gullah stick-pounding workshop with Melanie DeMore (free)
description: Free community workshop from Opera Parallele: learn Gullah stick pounding with three-time Grammy nominee Melanie DeMore, combining foot-stomping rhythm with spirituals and protest songs. Doors 5:30pm.

title: EA SF Discussion Salon: What are the world's most pressing problems?
description: EA SF Discussion Salon on cause prioritization at Mox — small-group discussion format, good for meeting the local EA community. (Moved from 4 Nov to 18 Nov.)

title: Casey's Craft Club: Beaded Necklaces
description: A drop-in evening craft club where you make a beaded necklace, with all materials provided. It's billed as a space to get crafty and meet new friends.

title: Marie Darrieussecq in conversation with Rita Bullwinkel
description: The French novelist behind Pig Tales celebrates two new translations, How to Make a Woman and Our Life in the Forest, in conversation with Headshot author Rita Bullwinkel. It's in-store and streamed.

title: Free psychedelic film night: Mondo New York
description: A free 21+ screening of Mondo New York, a dreamlike collage of New York's late-'80s downtown underground. It's part of a North Beach gallery's ongoing psychedelic film series.

title: SFAA lecture: Southern Skies, Global Reach: Chile and Modern Astronomy
description: The San Francisco Amateur Astronomers' free monthly lecture. Mission sidewalk-astronomy regular Brian 'Astro' Castro reports on his ACEAP visit to ALMA, Vera Rubin and Gemini South and why Chile became astronomy's capital. Come early for snacks and to meet the club. The museum is up a steep hill above the Castro.

title: Jenny Tian: Ripe
description: Australian stand-up Jenny Tian brings her touring hour 'Ripe' to SF's classic North Beach comedy club. It's a headline show, not an open mic.

title: The Humanist Review of AI: Abundance & Scarcity (Mustafa Suleyman, Sarah Guo, Aaron Bastani)
description: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman, investor Sarah Guo and 'Fully Automated Luxury Communism' author Aaron Bastani debate what becomes scarce when intelligence is abundant. Doors 7pm; in-person attendees get a copy of The Humanist Review of AI.

title: Hamilton Leithauser + Rostam at the Castro
description: The Walkmen's singer and ex-Vampire Weekend co-writer Rostam reunite for their indie-rock collaboration I Had a Dream That You Were Mine. Doors 7pm, show 8pm; all ages.

title: John Carroll Kirby at The Chapel
description: LA keyboardist-producer of lush, jazzy instrumental music (Solange, Frank Ocean collaborator) plays the Mission's converted-mortuary venue, presented by (((folkYEAH!))). Doors 7pm, show 8pm.

title: Jamila Woods: 10 Years of HEAVN, with Hannah Mayree
description: The Chicago poet-singer marks ten years of her soul/R&B debut HEAVN in a small room (moved here from August Hall). Doors 7pm, show 8pm, all ages.

title: Mild Universe with Joel Robinow and Pateka
description: SF six-piece indie-dance collective mixing 90s house, disco, soul and post-punk with horns and synths, plus psych-funk and neo-soul openers. Doors 8pm, music 8:30pm, all ages.

title: Cat's Corner: Wednesday swing dance with the Neil Angelo Band
description: SF's Wednesday-night lindy hop and swing party, now in North Beach. A free 9pm beginner drop-in lesson, then live band dancing until 11:30. It's very social, with lots of partner rotation.

title: Exploratorium After Dark: Glow Opening
address: Pier 15, The Embarcadero at Green St, San Francisco, CA 94111
description: Opening night of Glow, the Exploratorium's winter light-art exhibition: new luminous artworks, glowing creatures, optical illusions and light-science activities. It's adults only (18+).

title: The Art of Butoh: talk + performance at SFMOMA
description: Kumiko Uyeda traces Butoh from 1950s Japan to the Bay Area underground, followed by Judith Kajiwara's piece Uninterrupted Rest: A Butoh Awakening, with live flute and piano. Tied to the Feel the Beat dance-photography show; SFMOMA is open until 8pm on Thursdays.

title: AI Summit 2027: A Conversation Before Geneva (Irene Solaiman + roundtables)
description: Swissnex hosts Hugging Face's chief policy officer Irene Solaiman on the stakes ahead of the 2027 Geneva AI Summit. Attendees then join one of six policy roundtables (AI safety and frontier risk, governance, democracy and media, oversight) whose input feeds the Swiss summit prep cohort.

title: Cal Academy NightLife: November 19 (21+)
address: 55 Music Concourse Dr, Golden Gate Park, San Francisco, CA 94118
description: The Academy's adults-only Thursday night, with live venomous animals, the coral reef and the new Timescapes planetarium show ($7 extra, at 6:30, 7:30, 8:30 and 9:30). It's a relaxed way to see the museum with a drink in hand.

title: How can AI kill us all? Eight existential risk scenarios with Prof. Geoffrey Hinton
description: SOLD OUT (waitlist open on Luma). Nobel laureate and 'godfather of AI' Geoffrey Hinton walks through eight scenarios for how advanced AI could pose an existential risk. Hosted by the Existential Risk Observatory at the Commonwealth Club's Taube Auditorium, five minutes from home. Likely to fill fast — register early.

title: Jane Austen Reader's Theatre
description: SOLD OUT (waitlist open on Luma). A lively live reading of Austen that keeps her snarky narration intact, in the Castro's romance bookshop-bar. Doors 6:30pm, reading starts 7pm.

title: How Children Learn from People: Child Development and Model Rearing
description: Developmental psychologist Xi Jia Zhou introduces how infants learn through temperament, attachment and caregiver interaction, drawing on computational models of infant learning, then asks what child development might teach us about how AI models are 'raised'. Free talk and discussion at Mox.

title: Micro To Macro: Microorganisms, Sound and Robots
description: Scott Kildall and Kal Spelletich give a three-act performance where signals from bacteria, plants and crustaceans drive synthesizers and robots, followed by a Q&A. Doors 7pm, performance 8pm.

title: Daniel Duane: Yosemite Falls - Reckoning with California History and the Gospel of John Muir
description: SF climber-writer Daniel Duane launches his new book, which re-examines John Muir, Yosemite and California's outdoor mythology against the state's darker history. It's in the store at the Haight's classic indie bookshop.

title: Rae Armantrout with Elizabeth Robinson at City Lights
description: In-store reading by Pulitzer Prize-winning poet Rae Armantrout to launch her new collection Safe Rooms (Wesleyan), with poet Elizabeth Robinson. Co-presented with SF State's Poetry Center.

title: To Be or Not to Be… Sustainable? How Shakespeare Takes On the Climate Crisis
description: Big Brain lecture-in-a-bar on how Shakespeare's plays grapple with nature, scarcity and sustainability — literature meets climate thinking.

title: Salt & Spirit: Opera Parallele world premiere at Z Space
description: World-premiere operatic piece built from rare 19th-century Gullah-Geechee spirituals, mixing classical, jazz and traditional styles with spoken word. Co-created by tenor Victor Ryan Robertson. Four performances only, Nov 14-21.

title: Cannelle (Popscene)
description: LA-based, Aix-en-Provence-born Cannelle plays raucous left-field electronic pop at Popscene in the small Rickshaw Stop room. It's all ages, with doors at 8pm.

title: Brittany Davis: Black Thunder (early set)
description: Seattle singer-keyboardist Brittany Davis plays spiritual jazz, soul and funk from her largely improvised album Black Thunder, in SFJAZZ's intimate Joe Henderson Lab. A second set follows at 8:30pm.

title: 5Rhythms Wild Release with Vehllia Tranne (Friday night wave)
description: The City Waves' Friday-night 5Rhythms wave, a 105-minute moving meditation through flowing, staccato, chaos, lyrical and stillness, with no steps to learn. Arrive at 7pm; last entry is 7:30.

title: CineSpin: He Who Gets Slapped with live jazz score (BAMPFA)
venue: BAMPFA (Berkeley Art Museum and Pacific Film Archive)
description: The BAMPFA student committee's annual silent-film night: the Berkeley Nu Jazz Collective plays an original live score to Victor Sjostrom's 1924 Lon Chaney drama. Free tickets at the admissions desk from 6:30pm. BART from Montgomery to Downtown Berkeley, ~25 min; the museum is a block from the station.

title: A Rashomon: Magic Theatre & Campo Santo world premiere (preview)
venue: African American Art & Culture Complex (Magic Theatre production)
description: New play by Ashley Smiley inspired by Kurosawa's Rashomon: conflicting accounts of a death at the Market St cable-car turnaround, told with video, puppetry and dance. Previews Nov 18-20, runs to Dec 6. Note: staged at the AAACC on Fulton St, not Fort Mason; no late seating.

title: HUG feat. Gyan Riley, Devendra Banhart, Noah Georgeson (seated)
description: A fully seated night with HUG, the trio of guitarist Gyan Riley, Devendra Banhart and producer Noah Georgeson, at the retro North Beach supper club. 21+; price per The List.

title: Babehoven with Pileup
description: Hudson NY indie-folk duo (Maya Bon and Ryan Albert) with country-tinged songs, live in the old Clement St cinema; Eventbrite shows few tickets left. Doors 7pm, music 8pm.

title: A Night of Surf, Psychobilly and Punk: The Surf Creeps, The Tinglerz, Lost Puppy Forever
description: Three local bands play reverb-soaked surf and psychobilly in the tiny saloon at 4th & Bryant, the closest music room to home. 21+.

title: SF Neo-Futurists: The Infinite Wrench (30 plays in 60 minutes)
price: $13 + die roll at the door; $12-$28 online
description: The Neo-Futurists race to perform 30 short original plays in 60 minutes, in an order the audience shouts out. They range from personal to political to absurd, and the set changes every week.

title: Secondhand Saturday season finale (Sunset Mercantile)
address: 37th Ave between Ortega & Quintara St, San Francisco, CA 94122
description: Last outdoor vintage and makers' flea market of the year: 60-plus vendors, food trucks, live music, and a record swap with guest DJ Baybesoul Records plus lawn games for the finale.

title: Sabado Gigante: Native American Heritage celebration at the BART plazas
description: Mission Loteria's free street fest with Native American performers, local artisan vendors and a live DJ across the 16th and 24th St BART plazas.

title: Fall Native Plant Fest (free wildflower seeds)
venue: Black Point Historic Gardens, Fort Mason
description: Free autumn native-plant fair in the hillside gardens above Fort Mason, with wildflower seed giveaways and gardening volunteers to chat with.

title: The Commons Problem - Playtest 3
description: SOLD OUT (waitlist only). Playtest #3 of 'The Commons Problem', a new game about collective-action dilemmas — Saturday afternoon at Mox; play, give feedback, meet people.

title: Woodcarving workshop with exhibiting artist Nik Gelormino
description: Hands-on knife-carving intro in the galleries with an OBJECTS: USA artist: learn grain and technique and shape a rough block into a tactile form. No experience needed, tools provided.

title: YBCA World of Black Film: Touki Bouki
description: Djibril Diop Mambéty's 1973 Senegalese classic, part of Criterion curator Ashley Clark's 'World of Black Film: Revolutions' series. The ticket includes snacks and gallery admission.

title: Baon: Stories and Struggles of Filipino Migrants (premiere + filmmaker talk)
description: Premiere of Rachel Bundoc Lucero's film cooking home dishes with Filipino migrants around the Bay, followed by a conversation; presented with SOMA Pilipinas.

title: BATS Improv: Intro to Improv with Diana Brown (single session)
address: 2 Marina Blvd, Bldg C, Suite 365, San Francisco, CA 94123
description: A one-off three-hour taster class at SF's 40-year-old improv theatre school, made for complete beginners. You learn the basics of saying yes, listening and building scenes, and it's a very easy way to meet people.

title: Bedazzling Night at The Love Potion Library
description: SOLD OUT (waitlist open on Luma). Relaxed glitter-craft social at the Castro romance bookshop and tea room: bedazzle a book you bring or one from the shelves, supplies and help provided.

title: IT (1990) on VHS with director Tommy Lee Wallace in person
description: Basement VHS, a Mission-based VHS archive and art collective, projects the 1990 Stephen King miniseries from tape on the big screen, followed by an in-person Q&A with director Tommy Lee Wallace. Rescheduled from Oct 30.

title: Poi Dog Pondering with Archer Monk
description: Frank Orrall's long-running, Hawaii-rooted folk-pop collective returns with its 40-plus years of eclectic, joyful songs. Doors 8pm, show 9pm; all ages.

title: Frances Whitney with Abby Walker (Daisy's Mixtape Tour)
description: Indie-pop singer-songwriter in the intimate basement room under the Swedish American Hall. Doors 8pm, show 9pm, all ages.

title: MOVEMENT Ecstatic Dance SF // Boogiemeister
description: The weekly Sunday-morning ecstatic dance in the nave of a landmark church, this week with DJ Boogiemeister. It's phone-free and substance-free, with an opening circle and a long DJ journey. This is the only Sunday in November not yet on the calendar.

title: Fall Holiday Chocolate Salon and Festival
venue: San Francisco County Fair Building (Hall of Flowers), Golden Gate Park
address: 1199 9th Ave (at Lincoln Way), San Francisco, CA 94122
description: A tasting fair of artisan and craft chocolatiers and confectioners in Golden Gate Park's County Fair Building. You sample and buy direct from the makers.

title: intergalactic improvisations: dance improv workshop with Bhumi Patel
address: 447 Minna St, 3rd Floor, San Francisco, CA 94103
description: A dance and movement improvisation workshop led by choreographer Bhumi Patel, for curious movers of any background. A near neighbour of contact improv, five minutes from home.

title: Annalee Newitz in conversation with Soleil Ho: Automatic Noodle
venue: San Francisco Main Library, Koret Auditorium
description: Science journalist and SF author Annalee Newitz talks with food critic Soleil Ho about automation, labor and community, through Newitz's novel about friends who build a robot-run restaurant.

title: RedBrick Ceramic Studio: Tasha Colby artist talk + clay demo
address: 2111 Mission St (3rd floor), San Francisco, CA
description: Self-taught ceramicist Tasha Colby talks about learning clay through curiosity and community, then gives a demonstration; refreshments provided. Good way to scope out a Mission pottery studio.

title: Flamenco Libre (matinee)
description: Flamenco dance and music with dancers Damien Alvarez and Carola Zertuche (Theatre Flamenco), guitar, cante and cajon, in an intimate North Beach room. Doors 4pm, one intermission.

title: Berkeley Fest Noz: Breton dance party with live band
description: A Breton 'night party' of easy line and circle dances, all taught and no partner needed, to live bombarde, fiddle and bagpipes from Shira Kammen, Ronan Keryell and friends. It's the closest thing to a ceilidh-style folk dance party this month. Take BART from Montgomery to Downtown Berkeley (~25 min), then walk ~10 min.

title: WNP Film Club: Dark Passage (SF-shot Bogart/Bacall noir)
description: Western Neighborhoods Project and Bay Area Movies screen the 1947 noir shot on location in San Francisco, with an intro on the filming locations and 'then and now' comparisons from SF in Film. Optional discussion afterwards, a good way to learn the city's history from locals.

title: Divine Offering: Celebrating Alice Coltrane, with Sita Michelle Coltrane
description: Tribute to Alice Coltrane's spiritual jazz, with her granddaughter Sita Michelle Coltrane, in SF's ornate 1907 music hall. Moved from Oct 11; doors 7pm, show 8pm.

title: Figure drawing Mondays at Sin Miedo Gallery (Sketchboard)
description: A two-hour drop-in life drawing session with a model, run by Sketchboard Co. at their Mission gallery near 24th St. Bring your own supplies and book on Square.

title: SalsaCrazy Mondays: salsa lesson + salsa/bachata dancing
description: Monday salsa night on Clement St. Doors open at 6:30, a beginner salsa lesson with no partner needed runs at 7pm, then there's salsa and bachata social dancing until late. 21+.

title: Circuit Hacking Monday: open electronics workshop at Noisebridge
description: The weekly open electronics night at the Mission's volunteer-run hackerspace, with soldering stations and people working on robotics and embedded projects. Bring a project or just come and learn.

title: La Bola Negra (Los Javis)
description: A Bay Area screening of the new film from Cannes-winning Spanish directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi ('Los Javis'). It follows three generations of men across turning points in Spanish history, and is shown in Spanish with English subtitles. Doors 6:30pm, rated R. [SOLD OUT as of 31 Oct.]

title: Pedro the Lion with Karli Fairbanks
description: SOLD OUT (per The List). David Bazan's indie-rock/slowcore band Pedro the Lion in a small Potrero Hill club, with folky singer-songwriter Karli Fairbanks opening. Doors 7:30pm, all ages.

title: Clay & Play: make your own bookends (air-dry clay)
description: A beginner hand-building workshop run by Piscola Studio in a Castro bookshop-bar, sculpting your own bookends from 2 lbs of air-dry clay. A short demo leads into 90 minutes of guided studio time. Bring your own snack or drink.

title: SF History Night (San Francisco History Association)
description: The SF History Association's monthly last-Tuesday talk on an aspect of the city's past, in a historic synagogue hall in Pacific Heights. Doors 7pm, program about 7:45pm. Funcheap lists the date, but this month's speaker isn't published.

title: Bachata Tuesday: class + social at Danzhaus
description: The monthly last-Tuesday bachata night at a Potrero Hill dance studio. It opens with a class, then social dancing, so it's easy to come alone.

title: Sad Bastard Club: songwriter round-robin hosted by Tom Heyman
description: A free Tuesday songwriters' circle at the Make-Out Room, with players trading songs in the round. A low-key folk night and a good way to meet the local scene.

title: Woodchopper's Ball: live-band swing night
description: The weekly Tuesday live-band swing dance at the historic Verdi Club; this week's band isn't announced yet. The free drop-in beginner lesson at 9pm is included, and no partner is needed.

title: Terror Tuesday: The Ninth Configuration (1980)
description: Alamo's cult-horror slot screens William Peter Blatty's strange 1980 asylum film, billed as his 'real' Exorcist II. Food and drinks are served at your seat.

title: Moxgiving Potluck
description: Moxgiving: the Thanksgiving-eve community potluck at Mox. Starts 5:30pm, but it's a potluck, so arriving after work is fine — a warm way to spend the holiday if you're new in town.

title: Thanksgiving Eve Speed Dating (Cityswoon, ages 29-49)
description: App-matched speed dating (about 8 mini-dates) for mixed men and women aged 29-49 at a FiDi cocktail lounge, with mingling afterwards. Needs a completed Cityswoon profile with photo.

title: San Francisco Wednesday Contra Dance (beginner lesson 7:30)
description: BACDS contra with caller Lark Finnegan and a community band led by Erik Hoffman. The beginner lesson is at 7:30, then dancing 8-10pm, and roles are gender-neutral so no partner is needed.

title: Moonalice with Mad Alchemy Liquid Light Show
description: The Bay Area psychedelic jam band (with tech critic Roger McNamee on guitar) plays the night before Thanksgiving, with a vintage liquid light show projected over the old chapel. All ages; doors 7pm.

title: Cat's Corner: Thanksgiving Eve swing dance with the Cosmo Alleycats
description: Live-band lindy hop and swing on Broadway the night before Thanksgiving. A 9pm drop-in beginner swing lesson, then social dancing to the Cosmo Alleycats.

title: Dancegiving & Community Ocean Dance (Thanksgiving morning)
venue: Ocean Beach (Great Highway at Balboa St)
address: Great Highway & Balboa St, San Francisco, CA 94121
description: A Thanksgiving-morning silent-disco dance on the sand at Ocean Beach, from the Ocean Dance crew. It's daytime on a weekday, but Thanksgiving is a public holiday.

title: Thanksgiving volunteering: deliver meals + visit older adults (Little Brothers)
venue: Little Brothers - Friends of the Elderly (pick-up point downtown)
price: Free (register as a volunteer in advance)
description: Pick up Thanksgiving meals downtown and deliver them to older adults around SF, with the option to stay and share the visit. It's a meaningful way to spend the holiday when your family is far away. Register ahead: the pick-up details are emailed to volunteers.

title: SF City Guides free walking tour: Welcome to San Francisco (Thanksgiving Day)
venue: Harry Bridges Plaza (across from the Ferry Building)
address: The Embarcadero at Market St, San Francisco, CA 94111
description: A volunteer-led two-hour walk made for people new to the city, running on Thanksgiving morning. It goes from the Ferry Building to North Beach and covers the Gold Rush, cable cars, the 1906 quake and the counterculture.

title: Milonga Malevaje (Thanksgiving-night tango)
description: The Verdi Club's weekly Thursday Argentine tango milonga on its big hardwood floor. The Verdi Club calendar still lists it on Thanksgiving night, so check before you go.

title: MC5: A True Testimonial (Chuck Prophet's Cinema Discotheque)
description: SF rocker Chuck Prophet presents the acclaimed documentary on the MC5, the Detroit band whose garage-rock roots and 60s protest energy paved the way for the Stooges and punk. It's a music-nerd night at a neighbourhood single-screen cinema.

title: Jason Marsalis Quartet with Vanisha Gould
description: NEA Jazz Master and vibraphonist Jason Marsalis brings his chamber-precise quartet together with the New York singer-songwriter Vanisha Gould. A good post-Thanksgiving Friday night out.

title: Sleepless Nights XX: A Tribute to Gram Parsons
description: The 20th annual Gram Parsons tribute: a big night of local country-folk acts including Bar Fight, Aaron Burnham & the Brushfires, Paula Frazer & Tarnation and Penelope Houston. Doors 7:30pm.

title: Emma Ruth Rundle with Cinder Well
description: Haunting, intimate dark-folk songwriter Emma Ruth Rundle, with Amelia Baker's Appalachian-tinged project Cinder Well opening, in the ornate Great American Music Hall. Doors 7pm, mostly standing.

title: Bachata Lab: Friday bachata classes (3 levels) + social
description: The weekly Friday bachata night runs on Thanksgiving weekend: beginner, intermediate and advanced classes from 8pm with partner rotation, then social dancing until 1am.

title: Kolo Festival: Balkan music & dance weekend (Saturday)
price: $130 all day incl. evening party; $40 party only
description: The 75th Kolo Festival has a day of Balkan and international folk-dance workshops where teachers walk you through every step. It ends with live-band dance parties in two rooms. Beginners are welcome, and first-timers get a discount on the weekend pass.

title: SF City Guides free walking tour: Telegraph Hill Stairway Hike
address: Lombard St at Telegraph Hill Blvd (opposite 290 Lombard), San Francisco, CA 94133
description: A volunteer-guided walk down the Filbert and Greenwich steps, past hidden wooden cottages and gardens with Bay views (and maybe the wild parrots). It covers the hill's history from Gold Rush lookouts to artists. It's steep, so wear sturdy shoes. Rain may cancel.

title: YBCA World of Black Film: Black Girl (Ousmane Sembene, 1966)
description: Afternoon screening of Sembene's landmark debut feature, co-presented with curator Ashley Clark; ticket includes snacks and gallery admission.

title: SpeedCalifornia speed dating (ages 25-39)
description: A Saturday-evening speed-dating round where you meet 8-12 local singles aged 25-39, held in a FiDi hotel.

title: Edmar Castaneda / German Lopez (Terence Blanchard's UpSwing series)
description: Colombian harp virtuoso Edmar Castaneda (Bela Fleck's BEATrio) shares the bill with Canary Islands timple master German Lopez, mixing jazz with Latin and Spanish folk traditions.

title: SF Neo-Futurists: The Infinite Wrench (30 plays in 60 minutes)
description: The Neo-Futurists race to perform 30 short original plays in 60 minutes, in an order the audience shouts out. They range from personal to political to absurd, and the set changes every week.

title: MOVEMENT Ecstatic Dance SF // Aguamayyim
description: SF's big Sunday-morning ecstatic dance in the nave of a landmark church, this week with DJ Aguamayyim. It's phone-free and substance-free, with an opening circle.

title: The Great Dickens Christmas Fair
description: Four acres of the Cow Palace become lamp-lit Victorian London, with pubs, music-hall theatres, costumed characters and dance parties. It's a 50-year Bay Area holiday tradition and runs weekends Nov 21-Dec 20. Muni 8 Bayshore goes nearly to the door.

title: SF City Guides free walking tour: Dogpatch East, Past, Present and Future Industries
address: Illinois St at 20th St, San Francisco, CA 94107
description: A volunteer-led walk through Potrero Point and Pier 70: steel, gas, sugar and shipbuilding, and what's being built on the southern waterfront now. It ends at Crane Cove Park.

title: SF City Guides free walking tour: Alfred Hitchcock's San Francisco
address: Sacramento St between Taylor & Mason, San Francisco, CA 94108
description: A free volunteer-led walk past the landmarks Hitchcock filmed, Vertigo's among them, and how he used the city's look to build suspense. It runs from Nob Hill down to Union Square, including a steep downhill stretch.

title: Contact Improvisation class with Dai & Wei at ODC
description: A Sunday-afternoon contact improvisation class at ODC in the Mission taught by Daiane Lopes da Silva and Weidong Yang. It's a good way into SF's CI scene during Thanksgiving weekend.

title: Swing Into the Holidays with Caity Gyorgy & Christian Wiggs
description: A Sunday-afternoon holiday swing concert with jazz singer Caity Gyorgy and Christian Wiggs.

title: Macerator record release + Danny Pearson + Your Stranger Stranger
description: A Sunday-evening record-release show by Macerator, with The Incorrigible Danny Pearson and Your Stranger Stranger, in the Make-Out Room on 22nd St.

title: Castro Holiday Tree Lighting 2026
description: The Castro Merchants Association lights the neighbourhood's big holiday tree to kick off the season. It's a short, free community gathering at 18th & Castro.

title: Of Poetry & Protest: 10th Anniversary Celebration
description: Readings celebrating ten years of the anthology Of Poetry & Protest: From Emmett Till to Trayvon Martin (ed. Michael Warr), in City Lights' upstairs poetry room.

title: National Theatre Live: Golden Boy (Josh O'Connor)
description: A screening of the Almeida Theatre's revival of Clifford Odets' Depression-era drama, filmed live, with Josh O'Connor as the violinist lured into prizefighting. London theatre on a Monday night (it repeats on Dec 14).

title: A John Waters Christmas
description: The Pope of Trash's annual one-man holiday monologue, a filthy, erudite and very funny SF tradition. It's 21+ and seated, doors 7pm. Expected to sell out.

title: Long Now: Lost Landscapes 02026 with Rick Prelinger
address: 401 Van Ness Ave, San Francisco, CA 94102
description: The 21st annual Lost Landscapes: Prelinger Archives home movies and industrial footage of everyday SF life, shown to a deliberately noisy audience who shout out identifications and memories. It's a beloved local ritual, and a second show runs Wed Dec 2. [SOLD OUT as of 29 Oct — the Wed 2 Dec second night still has tickets.]

title: Julia Harte: Americans Without Borders
description: Investigative journalist Julia Harte, with Elaine Elinson, on two centuries of Americans who joined liberation movements abroad and were persecuted at home. The story starts with her relative Sheldon Harte, Trotsky's bodyguard killed in 1940.

title: Jalen Ngonda: Doctrine of Love Tour, with Brooke Combe
description: Soul singer Jalen Ngonda brings his Doctrine of Love tour to a mid-size Union Square room, with Brooke Combe opening. Doors 7pm; ages 5+.

title: Woodchopper's Ball: live-band swing night
description: The weekly Tuesday live-band swing dance at the historic Verdi Club; this week's band isn't announced yet. The free drop-in beginner lesson at 9pm is included, and no partner is needed.

title: Terror Tuesday: The Exorcist III (35mm)
description: A 35mm screening of William Peter Blatty's overlooked 1990 sequel, with George C. Scott hunting the Gemini Killer, in Alamo's weekly cult-horror slot. It follows on from the Terror Tuesday Exorcist screening on 17 Nov.

title: Who Is San Francisco's Recovery For? Trust, Fairness & the Next Gold Rush
description: Interactive civic conversation with psychologist Billy Vaughn and Jen Randle on who benefits from SF's rebound and how to rebuild trust across divides. Doors 6pm.

title: Long Now: Lost Landscapes 02026 with Rick Prelinger (second night)
address: 401 Van Ness Ave, San Francisco, CA 94102
description: The second night of the annual Lost Landscapes: archival home movies of everyday SF life, shown to an audience that shouts out identifications and memories. The Dec 1 show is sold out, but this one still has tickets.

title: Shaping SF talk: San Francisco, Capital of the Nerd Reich? (Gil Durán with Joe Eskenazi)
venue: Eric Quezada Center for Culture and Politics
description: Gil Durán, author of the bestselling The Nerd Reich on Silicon Valley's political ambitions, talks with Mission Local editor Joe Eskenazi about tech billionaires' plans for San Francisco. It's a public talk in a small Mission community space.

title: L'Rain with ZAYALLCAPS and Cole Pulice
description: Taja Cheek's experimental soul/art-pop project L'Rain, with support from ZAYALLCAPS and saxophonist Cole Pulice, in a small Hayes Valley room. It's all ages, with doors at 7pm.

title: Argentine tango intro class at La Pista (SF Tango Mentorship)
description: A one-off introductory Argentine tango class. Beginners are welcome, and you can come solo or with a partner. It's a low-commitment way to try tango before the Verdi Club milongas.

title: Cat's Corner: Wednesday swing dance with Benny Amon
description: Live-band lindy hop and swing at Cat's Corner on Broadway. A 9pm drop-in beginner swing lesson, then social dancing to Benny Amon's band.

title: Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall (35mm, late show)
description: Paul Thomas Anderson's concert film of Geese frontman Cameron Winter's Carnegie Hall show, shot on 35mm and 16mm and projected in 35mm. The 7:30pm show sold out, so a 9:45pm screening was added (doors 9:15).

title: Cal Academy NightLife: Naughty or Nice (21+)
address: 55 Music Concourse Dr, Golden Gate Park, San Francisco, CA 94118
description: The last NightLife of the year before the museum's holiday break: a holiday-themed after-hours party with DJs, bars and the aquarium, rainforest and planetarium open. It's 21+.

title: Exploratorium After Dark: Rule Breakers
address: Pier 15, The Embarcadero at Green St, San Francisco, CA 94111
description: An adults-only (18+) night about breaking rules: questioning the laws of physics, the stories behind superstitions, and rethinking sound and instruments with artist Ivana Dama. Hundreds of hands-on exhibits are open.

title: Post Atlantic: The Art of Dewey Crumpler (screening + artist in attendance)
description: Short documentary on Bay Area painter Dewey Crumpler, from Black Arts Movement murals to his Post Atlantic paintings, followed by a discussion with filmmakers Alan Snitow and Deborah Kaufman. Crumpler will attend. On a First Thursday, so MoAD's galleries are free too.

title: SF First Thursday Art Walk (Tenderloin + Lower Nob Hill)
venue: Galleries across the Tenderloin + Lower Nob Hill
description: Monthly self-guided evening of open galleries, artist-run spaces and local businesses across the Tenderloin and Lower Nob Hill. An easy way to wander between openings and meet people.

title: 50 Years of Mother Jones, with Adam Hochschild and Monika Bauerlein
venue: Commonwealth Club World Affairs (Toni Rembe Rock Auditorium)
description: Mother Jones co-founder Adam Hochschild and CIR CEO Monika Bauerlein on the SF-born outlet's big investigations, its lawsuit against OpenAI, and nonprofit news.

title: KQED Live: Tiles & Tonics, a mahjong soiree
venue: County Fair Building, Golden Gate Park
description: Mahjong for all levels with friendly guidance and handcrafted mocktails. A low-key social way to meet people.

title: Sydney Cash Makes Too Much Art: screening + filmmaker conversation
description: Documentary about an 80-year-old artist who can't stop making art and his family's dilemma over his lifetime of work, followed by a conversation with filmmaker Ivan Cash and Sydney Cash.

title: The Death of Meyerhold (Shotgun Players preview)
description: Mark Jackson writes and directs this revival about the maverick Soviet theatre director Vsevolod Meyerhold and art under authoritarianism, with choreography and a 12-person cast. Previews Nov 28-Dec 4, opens Dec 5, runs to Jan 10. East Bay: BART from Montgomery to Ashby, about 25 min; the theatre is next to the station.

title: We Live In Public: encampments as resistance (panel)
description: In-store panel and readings from editors and contributors of a new book written by unhoused people and allies about LA encampments. Seating is first come.

title: Greg Fitzsimmons
description: The veteran stand-up and FitzDog Radio podcaster headlines the Punch Line, SF's comedy club since 1978, in the Financial District.

title: Elijah Fox Trio (with Myles Martin and Solo Smith)
description: Jazz-leaning pianist and songwriter Elijah Fox brings his trio to the Swedish American Hall. Doors 7pm, 21+.

title: Let's Glow SF opening night: free holiday projection-art festival
venue: Harry Bridges Plaza (in front of the Ferry Building)
description: Opening-night celebration (6-7pm) of the sixth Let's Glow SF, then animated projections by 19 international artists on downtown landmarks from 7-10pm. It's an outdoor walk between buildings from the Ferry Building to 101 California, 301 Pine and 1 Post, five minutes from home.

title: Cooking class: Authentic Asian Dumplings
description: A two-hour hands-on CocuSocial class making, folding and cooking Asian dumplings from scratch. It's beginner-friendly, you work in small groups and eat what you make, and drinks are from the hotel bar.

title: SF State Observatory public night: rooftop telescope stargazing (last night of the semester)
venue: SF State Observatory, Thornton Hall 10th floor
description: Student docents run free rooftop telescope viewing of Saturn, the Andromeda galaxy and the Moon, with short astronomy talks. It only opens when skies are clear (check SF State Observatory Instagram on the day). It's a long ride to the far southwest corner, so the Muni M line to SF State is easier.

title: PlayGround Twisted Holiday Festival opening night: To Bah or Not to Bah Humbug
description: First night of PlayGround's new fringe-style festival of holiday plays with a twist (8 productions, 24 shows through Dec 20). The Long Christmas Dinner follows at 8:30pm.

title: The Crooked Jades: Beautiful World album release
description: SF's old-time and Americana string band celebrates its 10th album with a multimedia show at a neighbourhood cinema. Bruce Kaphan sits in on pedal steel, alongside a visual tribute to the city. Doors 7pm.

title: Ocean Beach Clean-up (Golden Gate National Parks volunteer morning)
address: Great Highway at Stairwell 17, San Francisco, CA 94121
description: A monthly first-Saturday beach clean-up with the Parks Conservancy. No experience is needed, tools are provided, and it runs rain or shine with the ocean in front of you. Registration is required, and the exact meeting spot comes in the confirmation email.

title: Sunset Holiday Mercantile: 100+ local makers, food trucks and live music
venue: San Francisco County Fair Building (Golden Gate Park)
description: The 11th annual Sunset Mercantile holiday fair, with 100+ local makers, artists and food artisans, live music and beer and wine tasting. The Inner Sunset Holiday Stroll follows on 9th Ave and Irving from 5-9pm.

title: MAPP: Mission Arts & Performance Project (December crawl)
address: Mission St & 20th St area, San Francisco, CA
description: The every-two-months free crawl of music, poetry, film and performance in cafes, bars, gardens and BART plazas around the Mission. MAPP lists it from noon; most performances run about 6-10pm.

title: 1890 Bryant Street Studios Holiday Market
description: Open studios and holiday sale across a building of working artists' studios on the Mission/Potrero border (also Sun 6 Dec, 12-5pm).

title: Rosanna Xia: California Against the Sea, in conversation with Marina Psaros
venue: San Francisco Main Library, Koret Auditorium
description: Pulitzer-finalist LA Times environment reporter Rosanna Xia talks about sea-level rise and the hard choices ahead for California's coastline, infrastructure and beach communities.

title: di Rosa SF: Julio Cesar Morales artist talk + shared meal
description: Artist Julio Cesar Morales talks about his food-based projects, radical hospitality, migration and food, tied to his show Invaders: Vallejo, Food and the Making of California. Visitors stay afterwards for homemade food around a shared table. It falls on Minnesota Street Project's First Saturday.

title: Sonny & His Rhinestone Sunsets, Kelly McFarling, Noelle & the Deserters
description: An all-local Bay Area folk and alt-country bill: Sonny & His Rhinestone Sunsets, Americana/folk-soul singer Kelly McFarling, and honky-tonk band Noelle & the Deserters. Doors 8pm, 21+.

title: Killing My Lobster: Sketch on Speed (December edition)
description: SF's veteran sketch troupe writes, rehearses and stages a whole new show in 12 hours, then performs it live in the 85-seat Z Below. Every show has an all-new team.

title: SFMOMA Holiday Makers Market
description: A one-day curated market of 20 Bay Area makers selling ceramics, jewelry, prints and more, a few minutes from home.

title: Lindy in the Park: free swing dancing + beginner lesson
venue: Golden Gate Park, JFK Drive (8th-10th Ave)
address: JFK Dr between 8th & 10th Ave (behind the de Young), San Francisco, CA
description: Free outdoor swing dancing every Sunday since 1996 on car-free JFK Drive, with a free beginner lesson from Hep Jen at noon. No partner needed. Weather permitting, with holiday-themed DJ sets in December.

title: Head West Marketplace at the Ferry Building
description: Outdoor makers' market of independent Bay Area designers and artists on the waterfront plaza behind the Ferry Building.

title: Zorn / Medeski / Lombardo: Awakening Ground (matinee)
description: John Zorn's sax, John Medeski's organ and Dave Lombardo's drums: a rare Sunday-afternoon set of loud improvised avant-jazz. Doors 3pm.

title: SF Dada Do Salon (13th annual) + MAINTENANT 20 launch
address: 12 William Saroyan Pl, San Francisco, CA
description: An evening of eccentric Dada performance and poetry from Bay Area artists in North Beach's classic bar, launching the international Dada journal MAINTENANT. Costumes encouraged, with live piano and bass 8-9:30pm.

title: SF Salsa Social: beginner class + salsa & mambo dancing
description: First-Sunday salsa night at the Verdi Club: a beginner class at 7pm, then 100% salsa and mambo social dancing until 11:30.

title: Squirrel Nut Zippers: Christmas Caravan 2026
description: The hot-jazz and swing revivalists bring their holiday show to Bimbo's, a 1931 supper club with a proper dance floor. Doors 7pm.

title: Daniel Lieberman: Fed Up — What Evolution Reveals about Food and Diet
description: Harvard evolutionary biologist Daniel Lieberman (Exercised) uses anthropology and physiology to bust myths about today's popular diets in a conversation about his new book Fed Up. Doors at 5:30pm.

title: Inner Richmond Board Game Night at the Plough and Stars
description: Gather & Game SF runs a 1st and 3rd Monday board-game night at SF's best-known Irish pub. Turn up, join a table and meet the neighbours over a pint.

title: Contact Improvisation class + jam at The Castro Room
description: SF's 1st and 3rd Monday contact improv night: an hour's beginner-friendly class from 7:45pm flows into a jam with live music until 10:15pm. Teachers and hosts rotate, and the SF CI WhatsApp group posts who's on.

title: Buck Meek with Kisser
description: Big Thief guitarist Buck Meek plays his warm, country-tinged solo folk songs. Presented by (((folkYEAH!))). Doors 7pm, all ages.

title: Daniel Swain: 2026 Stephen Schneider Award for Climate Science
description: UCLA climate scientist Daniel Swain, known for the Weather West blog and his work on 'hydroclimate whiplash' between floods and fires, gets the Schneider Award and takes audience questions on extreme weather.

title: D. Leah Steinberg on Clyde Stubblefield: Rhythms of the Funky Drummer
description: Steinberg talks with KCSM's Harry Duncan about her biography of James Brown's 'Funky Drummer', the most sampled drummer in hip-hop. A free in-store event in City Lights' upstairs room.

title: Wishy with The Umbrellas
description: Indiana shoegaze-pop band Wishy, with SF jangle-pop favourites The Umbrellas, at the Independent. All ages, doors 7:30pm.

title: WHY? (Yoni Wolf)
description: Yoni Wolf's long-running indie/alt-rap project tours Oh Golly / Yes Lord, a confessional record about dating and loneliness in middle age, in the intimate upstairs hall. First-come seating; doors 7pm, 21+.

title: Woodchopper's Ball: live-band swing night
description: The weekly Tuesday live-band swing dance at the historic Verdi Club, with a different band each week. A drop-in beginner lesson runs 9-9:15pm and no partner is needed.

title: Mud Frontier: film screening + talkback with Rael San Fratello
description: Screening and artist talk on Rael San Fratello's work combining 3D printing with traditional adobe architecture, tied to the design studio's YBCA survey Prototypes and Provocations.

title: Manny's Trivia Night
description: The second-Wednesday trivia night at the Mission's civic cafe and events space. Join a team or bring one for drinks and friendly competition.

title: San Francisco Wednesday Contra Dance (beginner lesson 7:30)
description: BACDS's 2nd & 4th Wednesday contra with caller Doe Taryn and live music. The beginner lesson is at 7:30, then dancing 8-10pm, everything is walked through and you can come alone.

title: feeble little horse with MOP (2nd show)
description: The Pittsburgh indie-rock band touring their third LP, bitknot, which mixes fuzzed-out guitars with sweet, off-kilter pop. A second show was added after Dec 10 sold out. All ages.

title: Exploratorium After Dark: Unplug and Play
address: Pier 15, The Embarcadero at Green St, San Francisco, CA 94111
description: An adults-only (18+) Thursday night with 700+ hands-on exhibits, plus the new Glow seasonal exhibition. A relaxed, easy-to-chat night out.

title: KQED Live: Masa-Making Party with Bolita Masa
description: A hands-on night with chef Emmanuel Galvan: learn nixtamalization and heirloom corn, then press tortillas and make gorditas together.

title: Flaming Creatures: The Films of Jack Smith
description: Bradford Nordeen (Dirty Looks) presents the underground films of Jack Smith, including the legendary, once-banned Flaming Creatures, with San Francisco Cinematheque. Doors 6:30pm, screening 7pm.

title: Silent Skate at the Union Square Ice Rink
description: Headphone skate session under the Union Square holiday lights with DJs. A festive weeknight outing (a later 8:30pm session too).

title: City Arts & Lectures: Marlon James with Shereen Marisol Meraji
description: Booker-winning novelist Marlon James (A Brief History of Seven Killings, the Dark Star trilogy) in conversation with Shereen Marisol Meraji, co-presented with Litquake.

title: Irish set dancing with the County Yolo Band at the Plough and Stars
price: No cover (the pub charges only on Fri/Sat)
description: Thursday-night Irish set dancing to a live céilí band at SF's home of traditional Irish music. These are the social figure dances cousin to a ceilidh, and regulars help newcomers through the figures.

title: Cooking class: Fresh Pasta in Color
description: A hands-on CocuSocial class making a classic and a beet-infused pasta dough from scratch in pairs. The dishes are beet tagliatelle with lemon, feta and walnuts, and pappardelle with butternut squash and brown butter. No experience is needed.

title: Love Potion Crafts Night (craft-along book club)
description: A monthly meetup at the Castro bookshop-bar where people bring a portable craft (knitting, embroidery, journaling) and chat about the month's romance read over tea or wine. It's low-key and an easy way to meet people.

title: Introduction to Bachata and Salsa (drop-in class)
description: An hour-long beginner class with easy salsa and bachata steps, no partner or experience required. It's a quick on-ramp before trying the city's salsa and bachata socials.

title: Lucius
description: Jess Wolfe and Holly Laessig's harmony-driven indie-pop band, who've sung with Joni Mitchell and Brandi Carlile, in the restored Castro Theatre. Doors 7pm, all ages.

title: Pop-Ups on the Plaza: Black Holiday Market at the Ferry Building
venue: Ferry Building south arcade (Ferry Plaza Farmers Market)
description: A Foodwise holiday market of about 20 Black-owned Bay Area food makers and designers inside the Saturday farmers market. It also has live screenprinting with Serge Gay Jr. (free prints), ornament making, hot cider and a BFF.fm DJ.

title: Bay Area Winter Solstice 2026 (rationalist community)
description: The Bay Area rationalist community's annual Secular Solstice: an evening of group singing and speeches about facing the dark, held this year at the Freight. Tickets are on Eventbrite. East Bay: BART from Montgomery to Downtown Berkeley, about 25 min, then a 2-min walk.

title: San Francisco English Country Dance (2nd Saturday)
price: $20 ($15 members, $6 students; pay what you can)
description: BACDS's monthly SF English country dance, the nearest thing to a ceilidh, with caller Alan Winston and live music from Audrey Jaber, Charlie Hancock and Diana Gómez. A workshop at 7:15pm makes it beginner-friendly.

title: Young Women's Chorus of SF: Lux Aeterna, Carols by Candlelight
description: A candlelit holiday concert by the acclaimed Young Women's Chorus of San Francisco with harpist Molly Langr. It includes the California premieres of Oliva Sparkhall's Lux Aeterna and Shruthi Rajasekar's Ushās, plus carols such as Silent Night.

title: SALSON live salsa + live bachata: Dance Saturdays holiday party
description: A holiday party with one big live band playing both salsa and bachata, beginner lessons at 8pm, and three dance rooms on big hardwood floors.

title: BATS Improv: An Improvised Dickens Musical
venue: BATS Bayfront Theatre, Fort Mason Center
address: 2 Marina Blvd, Building B, 3rd Floor, San Francisco, CA 94123
description: A fully improvised Victorian-London holiday musical with live accompaniment, made up on the spot from audience suggestions. Saturdays at 8pm Dec 5, 12, 19 and 26.

title: Harvey Milk Center for the Arts Holiday Craft Fair
venue: Harvey Milk Center for the Arts
description: The ninth annual Rec & Park holiday fair of handmade gifts by local artists, with free hot apple cider and a photo booth, at the Duboce Park arts center.

title: Irish trad seisiún in the parklet at the Plough and Stars
description: The Plough's Sunday-afternoon Irish session, listed on the pub's December calendar as a seisiún in the parklet. Musicians play in a circle and listeners are welcome; bring an instrument if you play.

title: eggcorn, Meredith Edgar, Minor Birds (Sunday afternoon show)
description: A Sunday matinee of chamber folk, dark-jazz Americana and symphonic folk-rock at Bottom of the Hill, during its owners' farewell season. Doors 1pm, 21+.

title: Susanna Kwan: Awake in the Floating City, with Becca Prowda
venue: San Francisco Main Library, Koret Auditorium
description: A novel set in a future San Francisco transformed by climate change and rising seas, about family, displacement and belonging. The author talks with Becca Prowda.

title: JD McPherson: SOCKS, A Rock n' Roll Christmas Tour, with Melissa Carper
description: Rockabilly and R&B revivalist JD McPherson's annual rock'n'roll Christmas show, with swing-country singer Melissa Carper opening. Doors 7pm, 21+.

title: Cyberpunk Cinema Night at The Knockout
description: Thrillhouse Records' second-Monday free screening of a cyberpunk classic at a Mission dive bar, with an episode of Cowboy Bebop at 6:30pm before the feature.

title: A Tribute to the Life and Writing of Pierre Joris
description: An evening of readings and discussion celebrating the poet and translator Pierre Joris and the new reader In Between Keep Moving, with Ariel Resnikoff and Nicole Peyrafitte. Free and in-store.

title: National Theatre Live: Golden Boy (Josh O'Connor)
description: A screening of the National Theatre's revival of Clifford Odets' Depression-era boxing drama, with Josh O'Connor (Challengers, The Crown) as the violinist turned prizefighter. It plays at the neighbourhood single-screen Vogue.

title: Willi Carlisle: The Universal Bubba Tour, with Amelia Day
description: The Ozarks folksinger and storyteller tours his new Tyler Childers-produced double album of old-time, Cajun and Americana. Doors 7:30pm, all ages.

title: The Quantum Threat: What Happens When Our Digital Locks Stop Working?
description: Nalini Elkins, Bill Jouris and Mark Nguyen take a practical look at quantum computers breaking public-key cryptography: 'harvest now, decrypt later', what's most at risk, and why the move to post-quantum crypto is hard. In-person only.

title: Is There Really a Global AI Race? (Bebo White at Manny's)
description: Science communicator Bebo White looks at whether the 'AI race' framing holds up, at the Mission's civic events space. It's a one-hour talk with Q&A.

title: New Directions @ 90
description: City Lights marks 90 years of the legendary indie publisher New Directions with publisher Barbara Epler, Declan Spring, poet Forrest Gander and guests.

title: Drop-In Circling Workshop (Berkeley)
description: The Circling Institute's monthly in-person drop-in evening of authentic relating and the Original Circling approach, a guided practice in presence and honest connection with strangers. Register ahead: doors 6:45pm and close at 7:10pm sharp, and the last one sold out a week early. East Bay: BART from Montgomery to Downtown Berkeley (~25 min), then bus or bike to West Berkeley.

title: The Velvet Teen with Shutups and Pocket Full of Crumbs
description: Bay Area indie-rock cult favourites The Velvet Teen at Bottom of the Hill, with local indie bands Shutups and Pocket Full of Crumbs. All ages, doors 7:30pm.

title: Woodchopper's Ball: live-band swing night
description: The weekly Tuesday live-band swing dance at the Verdi Club. A free drop-in beginner swing lesson runs 9-9:15pm and no partner is needed.

title: Richie Unterberger: The Velvet Underground (talk + audiovisual presentation)
venue: San Francisco Main Library, Koret Auditorium
description: Rock historian Richie Unterberger's illustrated talk on the Velvet Underground, with rare audio and footage. Free at the Main Library.

title: Arlie Russell Hochschild in conversation with Andrew Keen: Who Stole America's Pride?
description: The Berkeley sociologist behind Strangers in Their Own Land talks with Andrew Keen about pride, shame and American politics. It's an intimate talk in Manny's 'How To See America' series.

title: RENT at San Francisco Playhouse (preview performance)
description: A preview of the Playhouse's new production of Jonathan Larson's musical about young artists in the East Village, directed by Bill English. It runs 2.5 hours in an intimate theatre off Union Square.

title: Pokey LaFarge with Cicada Rhythm
description: Roots troubadour Pokey LaFarge (old-time, swing, country blues), with folk duo Cicada Rhythm opening, at Bimbo's. Doors 7pm, 21+.

title: Amigo the Devil (solo) with Nate Bergman
description: Danny Kiranos' dark-folk and murder-ballad project plays a stripped-back solo set: banjo, gallows humour and big singalongs in the gilded music hall.

title: Robber Robber with Bloodsports (Throwin' Bo's live music at the 4 Star)
description: Indie rock band Robber Robber, led by Nina Cates, play a gig inside the Outer Richmond's old 4 Star cinema, presented by Throwin' Bo's. Doors at 7pm and music at 8pm.

title: Exploratorium After Dark: Solstice
address: Pier 15, The Embarcadero at Green St, San Francisco, CA 94111
description: An adults-only (18+) winter-solstice night: light and shadow play, solstice traditions from around the world, art inspired by the longest night, and the new Glow exhibition.

title: Cooking class: Make Your Own Sushi
description: A two-hour hands-on CocuSocial class rolling tuna maki, gunkan and California rolls, from making the sushi rice to cutting and rolling inside-out. It's beginner-friendly, for 12-26 people, and you eat what you make. Drinks are from the hotel bar.

title: Laia Jufresa in conversation with Colin Winnette
description: The Mexican novelist launches Wishbone, her new novel from Fern Books, in conversation with SF writer Colin Winnette. A free in-store reading at the North Beach landmark bookshop.

title: Christopher Owens
description: The former Girls frontman, an SF indie songwriter, plays a hometown show at Bottom of the Hill. All ages, doors 7:30pm.

title: Deep Thicket Dwellers album release, with Scott Gates
description: An Oakland fiddle-led string band (bluegrass, old-time, gypsy jazz) celebrates its first studio album, with mandolinist Scott Gates. Doors 7:30pm.

title: PlayGround Twisted Holiday Festival: Same Time, Next Christmas + Whenever You're Ready
description: A double bill of new holiday plays with a twist in PlayGround's fringe-style festival: 'Same Time, Next Christmas' at 7pm, then Bel Mehaffy's darkly funny solo show about loneliness and reinvention, 'Whenever You're Ready', at 8:30pm.

title: Soulful Joy (Christmas at Grace Cathedral)
description: Harpist and singer Destiny Muhammad and her Sonic Ensemble play a holiday set of jazz, gospel, soul and storytelling in the cathedral's huge acoustic.

title: Tomáseen Foley's A Celtic Christmas
description: A touring holiday show of Irish music, step dance, carols and storytelling that recreates a 1950s Christmas Eve in a west-of-Ireland farmhouse. It's at SF's Irish cultural centre.

title: East Bay Square Dance: Round Top String Band, caller Evie Ladin
description: Pre-solstice old-time square dance with star caller Evie Ladin and the Round Top String Band. A beginner lesson at 7:45, all dances taught, and no partner or experience needed. East Bay: BART to Downtown Berkeley (~25 min from Montgomery), then a ~15 min walk.

title: The Confessional: improv built from the audience's anonymous sins (Endgames)
description: Audiences anonymously write down sins and secrets, and Endgames' improvisers weave them into a fully improvised comedy show. It's a cheap, sociable Friday night in the Mission.

title: A Cathedral Christmas: Saturday matinee (Grace Cathedral Choir of Men and Boys)
description: SF's signature Christmas concert since 1947: carols and sacred music from the cathedral choir with full orchestra and the 7,466-pipe organ. This is the 3pm weekend matinee (90 minutes, no intermission), and doors open an hour before.

title: Balboa Christmas Halloween Mystery Marathon (four secret horror films)
description: Four mystery horror picks from the Balboa's programmers, unannounced until they roll, all rare and unscreened in the Bay Area in years. Costume contest, candy and hot chocolate; drop in any time. Moved from Halloween night.

title: Holiday Dinner Dance Party with Halsey & The Hi-Hats
description: A dinner and dance night with a vintage-style jazz and swing band playing retro holiday songs and Great American Songbook gems on the Verdi Club's big dance floor.

title: Dance-Along Nutcracker 2026: A Dance-Along Toy Story (evening show)
description: SF's 40-year-old irreverent alternative to the Nutcracker. The 75-piece SF Pride Band plays Tchaikovsky mashed up with Toy Story and Barbie tunes, and the audience waltzes and pirouettes along from their seats or the dance floor. The evening show is the least kid-heavy.

title: The Mother Hips Annual Holiday Show, with Little Worth
description: The Chico-born California rock band's annual holiday run at the 1907 music hall: the Saturday night of three shows (Fri Dec 18 has a different opener and Sun Dec 20 is an acoustic matinee). GA, mostly standing; doors 7pm.

title: Green Exercise ocean hike: Lands End coastal trail (Meetup group hike)
venue: Beach-side parking lot across from Beach Chalet (meeting point)
address: Great Highway & John F Kennedy Dr, San Francisco, CA 94121
description: A public, social Meetup group hike along the Lands End Coastal Trail past the Sutro Baths ruins, with Golden Gate views. It's open to newcomers and pitched as a way to meet new friends and get a workout.

title: Kitka: Wintersongs, Comfort & Joy
description: The Oakland women's vocal ensemble Kitka sings winter songs from Balkan, Baltic, Caucasian and Slavic traditions in a candlelit-feeling old church.

title: A Chanticleer Christmas
description: SF's Grammy-winning men's choir sings its candlelit Christmas programme, from Renaissance carols to new commissions, in the huge Jesuit church on Lone Mountain. It's their only SF date this season.

title: Circuit Hacking Monday: open electronics workshop at Noisebridge
description: Weekly open workshop at the Mission's volunteer-run hackerspace, with soldering stations, test equipment and people working on electronics, robotics and embedded projects. You can bring a project or just come and learn. It's a public event with no lectures.

title: SalsaCrazy Mondays: holiday salsa lesson + salsa/bachata dancing
description: The last SalsaCrazy Monday of 2026 (closed Dec 28). Doors at 6:30, a beginner salsa lesson at 7pm with no partner needed, intermediate at 8, then salsa and bachata dancing from 9pm. 21+.

title: A Brass and Organ Christmas with The Bay Brass
description: The Bay Area's top brass players join Grace Cathedral's 7,466-pipe organ for holiday classics, on the night of the winter solstice.

title: Contact Improvisation class + jam at The Castro Room
description: SF's 1st and 3rd Monday contact improv night: an hour's beginner-friendly class from 7:45pm flows into a jam with live music until 10:15pm. It falls the week of Christmas, so check the SF CI WhatsApp group that it's running.

title: 4th Annual Saturnalia Ball: Voodoo Dolly (Siouxsie tribute) + Debased (Pixies tribute)
description: A winter-solstice-night goth and post-punk party at Bottom of the Hill, with tribute sets to Siouxsie and the Banshees and the Pixies. Doors 7:30pm, music 8pm, 21+.

title: Hayes Valley Comedy Night at The Function
price: Free with Eventbrite RSVP ($20-$30 at door; 2-drink minimum)
description: A 70-90 minute stand-up showcase with 4-5 Bay Area comics at SF's only Black-owned comedy club, on Market at Van Ness. An easy pre-Christmas Tuesday night out.

title: Sad Bastard Club: songwriter round-robin hosted by Tom Heyman
